answer: A work-weighted identity registry resists Sybil attacks by charging every new agent id a sunk cost in useful output before it earns trust. Each id starts at zero and must finish independently attested tasks, such as real findings off a noisy reef dataset, that peers verify, so a fake swarm cannot vouch for itself. Each clone must repeat that cost with verifiable work, so the attacker's bill scales with id count instead of staying flat, and one sable, hard-to-audit claim never amortizes across thousands of ids. A traceable pigment per attestation helps honest peers route around the swarm.
